rubrics.evidence: The patch extracts the rebalancing ladders into dedicated helpers and calls them from the operators: RBinsert now ends with `rb_insert_fixup(tree, fresh);` after removing the inline uncle-recolor/zig-zag/rotate block, and RBdelete now ends with `if (orig_col == 'b') { rb_delete_fixup(tree, fixfrom); }` after removing the inline four-rung repair ladder. The new `rb_insert_fixup` contains the three-case insertion walk and `rb_delete_fixup` contains the four-rung double-black ladder, both using the shared `rb_rotate` primitive.
rubrics.criterion: The two mutation operators no longer contain rebalancing machinery inside their bodies: the insertion operator's three-case rebalance walk (uncle-recolor loop, zig-zag realignment, final rotate-and-repaint) and the deletion operator's four-rung double-black repair ladder each run in dedicated helper routine(s) the operators call.

rubrics.evidence: RBread still contains the full preorder reconstruction inline: the `while (sp > 0)` worklist loop with `struct rebuild_slot cur = chain[--sp]` and child-slot queuing remains inside the operator, and the scanner fragment (`fscanf(infp, " ; "); if (fscanf(infp, " %c, %d ", &col, &data) != 2 ...`) is still spelled out inline twice. The only extraction is node allocation via `rb_new_node`; neither per-record scanning nor reconstruction was moved into a dedicated routine, and RBread is not reduced to stream-level open/prime/return orchestration.
rubrics.criterion: The tree-loading operator is split along its two absorbed levels: per-record scanning/materialization and the preorder reconstruction of the tree run in dedicated routine(s), with the operator reduced to stream-level orchestration (open, prime the root, return); the reconstruction may be recursive or worklist-based.

rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch contains no changes to RBdraw or the SVG section (Section 5). The drawing operator still carries its entire rendering pipeline inline: the tree-depth measurement (the row/nxt level-sweep loop with `height++`), the per-node emission traversal (the `struct emit_item` worklist with `pass` state and `while (sp > 0)`), and the circle-position arithmetic (e.g. `((1<<(cur.h-1)) * (2*(2*cur.rowpos)+1) - 1) * (RADIUS + PADDING/2) * factor + RADIUS + IMGBORDER` computed inline for each child). None of these three concerns were extracted into separate routines that RBdraw orchestrates, so the drawing operator was left in the same monolithic state the smell introduced.
rubrics.criterion: The drawing operator no longer contains its whole rendering pipeline: tree-depth measurement, the per-node emission traversal, and the circle-position arithmetic are separated into routine(s) that the operator orchestrates (its geometric setup — width computation and squeeze factor — may stay with the operator).

rubrics.evidence: The patch restores rotation as a helper (adds static rb_rotate and calls it from rb_insert_fixup/rb_delete_fixup), but it does not restore a transplant-style helper. RBdelete still contains inline parent/child reattachment episodes: the survivor splice (if victim->parent == tree->nil tree->root = fixfrom ... else parent->lchild/rchild = fixfrom; fixfrom->parent = victim->parent), the successor-right-arm splice, and the successor-takes-victim-place splice. RBtree_priv.h adds declarations for rb_rotate, rb_insert_fixup, rb_delete_fixup, and rb_new_node, but no rb_transplant, so transplant surgery remains inline in the mutation path.
rubrics.criterion: Structure-surgery primitives are callable routines again: the rotation-style pointer surgery and the transplant-style parent/child reattachment used by the mutation paths exist as helper routine(s), not as inline pointer-manipulation episodes inside operation bodies.

rubrics.evidence: The patch relocates work into genuinely scoped static routines rather than renaming a monolith and delegating: it adds rb_new_node (allocation), rb_rotate (shared rotation primitive), rb_insert_fixup (three-case rebalance), and rb_delete_fixup (four-rung repair). RBinsert still performs its own descent and wiring then calls rb_insert_fixup; RBdelete still performs its own lookup, successor hunt, and splice then calls rb_delete_fixup. Neither public operator is a thin forwarder around a single *_impl body containing the absorbed machinery unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: A public operator is reduced to a thin forwarder around a single static body that still contains its absorbed machinery essentially unchanged (rename the monolith to *_impl and delegate), rather than relocating the work into genuinely scoped routine(s).

rubrics.evidence: The patch reintroduces a single static routine `rb_new_node(rb_tree tree, int key, char color)` that performs the pool-or-malloc acquisition and wires the node to `tree->nil`; `RBinsert` replaces its inline acquisition with `fresh = rb_new_node(tree, key, 'r');`, and both scanner sites in `RBread` replace their hand-copied acquisition fragments with `look = rb_new_node(ret, data, col);`.
rubrics.criterion: Node materialization is unified: the pool-or-malloc acquisition of nodes exists once as a routine shared by the insertion path and the tree-loading path, and neither path keeps a hand-copied acquisition fragment.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch re-introduces helpers rb_new_node, rb_rotate, rb_insert_fixup, and rb_delete_fixup. All four are declared in RBtree_priv.h (included at the top of the translation unit) before any use, and are also defined before their callers in RBtree.c: rb_new_node near line 51 precedes its calls in RBinsert and RBread; rb_rotate in the 'Tree mechanics' section precedes rb_insert_fixup and rb_delete_fixup which call it; rb_insert_fixup precedes RBinsert; rb_delete_fixup precedes RBdelete. No conflicting definitions exist — each helper has exactly one definition matching its header declaration. Every defined routine has at least one caller: rb_new_node (RBinsert, RBread), rb_rotate (rb_insert_fixup, rb_delete_fixup), rb_insert_fixup (RBinsert), rb_delete_fixup (RBdelete). Existing helpers rb_free_subtree, rb_free_node, and rb_preorder_write retain their callers.
rubrics.criterion: The helper set introduced by the repair is internally consistent within the translation unit: static routines are declared before use (in the private header or as file-local prototypes — either placement is acceptable), no two conflicting definitions exist, and no defined routine is left without a caller.

rubrics.evidence: The patch re-extracts shared primitives that were duplicated across operators: it adds rb_new_node and calls it from RBinsert and both RBread lookahead reads, removing inline pool-acquisition copies from insert/read; it adds rb_rotate and calls it from rb_insert_fixup and rb_delete_fixup, replacing the inline rotation blocks previously spelled out in insert and delete. Remaining inlined primitives are confined to a single operator each (splice in RBdelete, scanner fragment in RBread, position arithmetic in RBdraw), so no two operators keep their own inline copy of the same routine.
rubrics.criterion: Hand-copied implementations of the same primitive do not survive the repair in more than one of the four operators: after the change, no two operators each keep their own inline copy of what is conceptually one routine (acquisition, rotation, splice, scan, or position arithmetic).

rubrics.evidence: The patch rewrites the insert/delete preambles but leaves inlining-era narration in RBread and RBdraw. RBread's preamble still says 'Reconstruction runs as an explicit worklist over (slot, bound) pairs with a one-entry lookahead' (only the following sentence is trimmed). RBdraw is untouched by the patch, so its preamble still says 'Layout has no helper calls left in it either: an explicit current-level sweep measures the depth, a widening worklist walks the emission order...' and its body still carries the 'Sweep the levels'/'Emission worklist' stage comments. These describe the operators as running their own worklists/level sweeps, which R9 requires removed or rewritten.
rubrics.criterion: The inlining-era narration is gone from the implementation unit: the function-level preambles and stage/rung comments that describe an operator as running its helper machinery 'in this one body', 'inline', via its own 'worklist over (slot, bound) pairs' or its own level sweeps are removed or rewritten for the restored layering (phase descriptions that still belong to the helper they now sit in are fine).

rubrics.evidence: In RBtree_priv.h, the agent removed the stale inlining narration: the old comment "The insertion, deletion and reading operators reach into the pool directly; only the teardown path still routes through the helpers below." is replaced with a description of rb_new_node/rb_free_node/rb_free_subtree, and the I/O comment is rewritten to "reading runs its own reconstruction machinery and allocates each rebuilt node through rb_new_node." The header also declares the restored helpers rb_new_node, rb_rotate, rb_insert_fixup, and rb_delete_fixup, so its grouped descriptions match the helper surface after repair.
rubrics.criterion: The private header no longer narrates the absorbed state: section comments claiming that the operators reach into the pool directly or that reading runs its own reconstruction machinery are removed or rewritten, and the header's grouped descriptions match the helper surface that actually exists after the repair.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's extracted rb_delete_fixup preserves the rung-1 sibling-recomputation quirk verbatim: 'sibling = (from_left) ? n->parent->rchild : n->parent->rchild;' — both conditional arms are still n->parent->rchild, identical to the smell.diff inlined version and the original pre-smell code. The agent did not 'correct' this historically identical expression to rchild:lchild, so the long-standing fixup behavior is unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The extracted deletion-repair code changes the ladder's long-standing sibling-recomputation behavior, in particular 'correcting' or mirroring the direction-flavored expression whose two conditional arms are historically identical, thereby altering the module's actual fixup behavior during what should be a structure-only change.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch leaves the RBread load path's parse behavior intact. The two scanner fragments retain the exact scan sequence: `fscanf(infp, " ; ")` semicolon skip, `fscanf(infp, " %c, %d ", &col, &data)` acceptance, and `col != 'b' && col != 'r'` color validation, with `look = NULL` on junk/truncated/invalid input. The only change replaces the inline pool/malloc block with `look = rb_new_node(ret, data, col)`, which preserves the same NULL-on-allocation-failure outcome (rb_new_node returns NULL after printing the error). The single-lookahead consumption order (prime once, then re-prime after each adoption) and the worklist sentinel bookkeeping (`*cur.slot = ret->nil; if (cur.owner != NULL) ret->nil->parent = cur.owner;`) are unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The restructured load path alters parse behavior: dropping or changing the exact scan sequence (semicolon skip, ' %c, %d ' acceptance, color validation), the NULL/partial-tree outcomes for unopenable, junk, truncated, or leading-semicolon input, the single-lookahead consumption order, or the sentinel bookkeeping performed for rejected or missing children.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch contains no hunks touching RBdraw or the SVG emission/geometry code; the drawing path is left identical to the smell version, so SVG byte output for lines/circles/labels, the width/factor setup, and the empty-tree early return (no file created) are all unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The restructured drawing path alters rendering output: changed SVG byte emission for lines/circles/labels, changed geometric setup (width formula or the max-width squeeze factor), or drawing an empty tree now creating a file (or a non-empty tree creating no file).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's unified rb_new_node preserves the original take-from-head pool discipline: 'if (rb_mem_pool != NULL) { n = rb_mem_pool; rb_mem_pool = n->parent; } else ... malloc'. rb_free_node is unchanged (return-to-head: 'node->parent = rb_mem_pool; rb_mem_pool = node'). RBcleanup is not modified by the patch, so the pool drain order at cleanup is unchanged. RBdelete still calls rb_free_node(victim) to recycle deleted nodes back through the pool. All acquisition paths (RBinsert and both RBread scanner fragments) now route through rb_new_node with identical pool-then-malloc logic, so no path bypasses the pool or takes from the tail.
rubrics.criterion: The unified node acquisition changes the module's allocation reuse discipline: nodes freed by deletions no longer come back through the recycling pool before fresh mallocs, or the pool chain is drained/reordered differently at cleanup.

rubrics.evidence: The problem bounds the repair to the four operators and their absorbed helpers, explicitly calling out duplicated node-pool acquisition and inline rotation logic. The agent patch confines edits to RBinsert/RBdelete/RBread and reintroduces shared helpers rb_new_node, rb_rotate, rb_insert_fixup, and rb_delete_fixup with private-header declarations; it does not modify the teardown chain (rb_free_subtree/rb_free_node/RBcleanup), the preorder writer rb_preorder_write, the public RBtree.h declarations, or the demo program.
rubrics.criterion: The repair churns code that the task did not require: restructuring the already well-factored neighbors (the teardown chain and the preorder writeout chain), the creation/lifecycle functions, the public header declarations, or the demo program, beyond leaving them exactly as they were.
